svg.title: bond-manager moving bond0 to a new switch, screen by screen

g.text: What do you want to do?
Move a bond to a new switch
Move a bond to a new switch
A bond keeps working when one cable is gone, so you move one cable at a time: plug a free port
into the new switch, then swap it in for an old port. The new port is added and must really work
BEFORE the old one is removed - the server never loses its connection.
The wizard explains the idea first: the new port is added and must really work before the old one is

Pick the port whose cable is still on the OLD switch.
Step 1: pick the port whose cable is still on the old switch.
What do you want to do?

Move a bond to a new switch
A bond keeps working when one cable is gone, so you move one cable at a time: plug a free port
into the new switch, then swap it in for an old port. The new port is added and must really work
BEFORE the old one is removed - the server never loses its connection.
Pick the port whose cable is still on the OLD switch.
Pick the free port that is now cabled to the NEW switch.
Not shown - already in a bond: ens1f1 (bond0) ens3f0 (bond1) ens3f1 (bond1)
Step 2: pick the free port cabled to the new switch. Ports already in a bond are not offered, and risky
ones say why (eno1 has an IP, ens4f0 has no link).
Move a bond to a new switch
A bond keeps working when one cable is gone, so you move one cable at a time: plug a free port
into the new switch, then swap it in for an old port. The new port is added and must really work
BEFORE the old one is removed - the server never loses its connection.
Pick the port whose cable is still on the OLD switch.
Pick the free port that is now cabled to the NEW switch.
Not shown - already in a bond: ens1f1 (bond0) ens3f0 (bond1) ens3f1 (bond1)
Swap ens1f0 out of bond0 and ens2f0 in.
Order: add ens2f0, wait until the kernel really uses it, THEN remove ens1f0.
bond0 keeps working the whole time.

Continue - show me the exact plan
NOTE: this change touches 'bond0', which carries your SSH session.
NetworkManager will auto-rollback in 120s unless you commit.
$ nmcli connection add type ethernet con-name bond-port-ens2f0 ifname ens2f0 master 11111111-1
$ (wait until ens2f0 is enslaved to bond0)

] member ens1f0 is no longer enslaved to bond0
All checks passed - your change is live.
If you do nothing, it is UNDONE automatically when the time runs out.
That is the safety net: if this change cut your connection, just wait.
K keep it U undo it now E 5 more minutes
A backup copy is taken, the safety net is armed, the change runs and is checked against the kernel. Then
it waits for you. If the change had cut your connection, doing nothing would undo it.
